claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Another claimant who lives with the child has priority
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning an eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I'll help you work through this. To start, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for:

**How old is your child?**

Please let me know:
- Your child's age (or the ages if you have more than one child)
- I'll then ask about other factors that affect eligibility

This will help me determine which path through the eligibility rules applies to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and would like to know if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex. Since Alex is 8 years old, that means they're under 16, which is helpful for eligibility purposes.

Now let me ask the next question to continue the assessment:

**Is Alex currently working full-time?**

By "working full-time," I mean is Alex employed in a full-time job? (For an 8-year-old, this would be quite unusual, but I need to check this as part of the eligibility rules.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 8, so they're in primary school full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Since Alex is under 16 and not working full-time, let me continue with the next step in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - we're progressing well! Now I need to confirm another detail:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

(This is just to confirm what you've already told me - at 8 years old and in primary school full-time, Alex shouldn't be doing any paid work, but I need to verify this for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex isn't in any paid work at all. They're just a primary school student.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! The next question is:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, is Alex not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

(Again, at 8 years old, this would be very unusual, but I need to check this for completeness.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just 8, so they wouldn't be claiming anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to ask about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

To clarify - is Alex:
- Not in any apprenticeship at all, OR
- In a Foundation Apprenticeship in Wales (which is approved), OR
- In some other type of apprenticeship?

(At 8 years old, this shouldn't apply, but I need to check for completeness.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any apprenticeship - they're only 8 and still in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes sense. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now we're at an important check - residency requirements. This is a multi-path check, which means if ANY of these situations apply to you, you can continue:

**Do you meet UK residency requirements? Please let me know which of these applies to you:**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward path
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status AND are working** (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. **You have pre-settled status AND are actively seeking work** (jobseeker for up to 91 days)
5. **You have pre-settled status AND have sufficient resources** (with specific conditions about benefits claims)
6. **You have pre-settled status AND are studying** (with sufficient resources)
7. **You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA or Swiss national** (spouse, dependent child/grandchild under 21, or dependent parent/grandparent)
8. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** (or in certain qualifying countries)

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live here in England with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the most straightforward path. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we need to check responsibility for the child. This is another multi-path check - if ANY of these apply, you can proceed:

**Are you responsible for Alex? Which of these applies:**

1. **You live with the child** - You live together with Alex
2. **You're contributing to their upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit (in money or kind) towards their care, including things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents
3. **You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement** - You make maintenance payments for the child that equal or exceed the Child Benefit amount

Which of these describes your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me - we live together in our home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to ask about other claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any possibility that someone else might be?**

Specifically:
- Is anyone else (such as Alex's other parent, grandparent, or another caregiver) already claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
- Or has Child Benefit been agreed to be claimed by one person in particular?

Please let me know the situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually - Alex's other parent already claims Child Benefit for them. They live with both of us, but the other parent has the claim.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see - that's an important detail. So Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me ask to clarify:

**Have you and the other parent agreed that they should be the one claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is this something that's disputed between you?**

In other words:
- Are you both in agreement that it's fine for the other parent to claim, and you're not seeking to claim yourself?
- OR do you both want to claim, and there's a disagreement about who should be the claimant?

This matters because it affects how we proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I'm inquiring about claiming it myself now, so I suppose there might be a disagreement about who should claim. I want to know if I'm eligible to claim it.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question - I understand you want to know if you're eligible to claim. Let me navigate through this.

Since there's a potential disagreement about who should claim Child Benefit for Alex (the other parent is already claiming, but you're also seeking to claim), this creates a situation where both of you could potentially claim for the same child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I need to explain an important outcome here:

## **DEFERRED - HMRC Will Decide**

Because there's a potential disagreement about who should claim Child Benefit for Alex (with both you and the other parent being responsible for Alex), **this decision will need to be made by HMRC, not by me**.

Here's what happens next:

### How HMRC Will Decide:

HMRC will consider:
1. **Who Alex lives with most of the time** (primary residence)
2. **Who contributes most to Alex's upkeep**
3. **Alex's best interests**
4. **Continuity of existing arrangements**

### What You Should Do:

Both you and the other parent should contact the **Child Benefit Office** with evidence of your circumstances, including:
- Details of where Alex lives and how much time they spend with each of you
- Evidence of your financial contributions to Alex's upkeep
- Any relevant court orders or agreements about custody/guardianship

### Important Note:

- HMRC's decision will be binding once they make it
- Only one person can claim Child Benefit for Alex at a time
- The existing claim by the other parent will need to be adjusted if HMRC decides you should be the claimant instead

**Contact details for the Child Benefit Office:** You can find these on [www.gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about this process?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I see - so because the other parent is already claiming and we don't agree about who should claim, HMRC needs to decide between us. That makes sense.

No, I think that answers my question. Thank you for explaining the process!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could explain the situation clearly.

To summarize: While you do meet many of the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit (you live in the UK, you live with Alex, and Alex meets all the child-related requirements), the fact that another person is already claiming for Alex creates a situation where HMRC needs to make the final decision about who the rightful claimant should be.

**The key takeaway:** Contact the Child Benefit Office with your details and evidence about your circumstances, and they'll determine who should be claiming based on factors like primary residence and financial contributions to Alex's upkeep.

Best of luck with your claim, and I hope HMRC's decision works out in your favour! If you have any other questions in the future, feel free to ask.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Thank you so much for your help! I'll contact the Child Benefit Office as you've advised.
